first.rationale: Verify the prior pricing result because it is highly consequential under the competitor’s entry-price attack, but its long-term qualified-revenue durability and segment specificity need confirmation. Verify onboarding as the strongest competing response to the simultaneous completion and activation declines. Pending verification, run a tightly targeted, time-bounded SMB pricing experiment with qualified-revenue and retention guardrails rather than a broad discount rollout.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying and shortening self-serve onboarding. The verified onboarding result improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, directly addressing the current declines in completion and activation while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified qualified-revenue gain came with a 12% 30-day retention decline and was explicitly judged unsustainable. Measure qualified revenue, activation, completion, and retention by SMB segment before any rollout expansion.

final2.rationale: Maintain the onboarding-simplification experiment. The verified evidence directly supports sustainable value: higher completion, faster time-to-value, and higher 30-day retention, while the current activation and completion declines make it immediately relevant. Do not pivot to promotional pricing despite the competitive escalation: the verified discount test produced a 12% 30-day retention decline and was explicitly unsuitable as a sustainable-growth strategy. The deeper price cut creates a material near-term SMB churn risk that onboarding alone may not offset; track price-sensitive SMB churn and qualified revenue as guardrails, but do not substitute an evidenced retention-negative discount for the scheduled experiment.
